subject: HarborBank: operational evidence and pen-test summary for VM questionnaire
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@harborbank.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Mitchell <tom.mitchell@harborbank.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 15:04:00 -0400
Subject: Vendor evidence for vulnerability management questionnaire

Hi Mina,

Thanks for agreeing to help us with HarborBank's security review. The procurement RFP team has a number of specific asks around vulnerability management in the questionnaire: SAST/DAST coverage, patching SLAs by severity, a summary of the most recent pen test (redacted where needed), and a current SBOM snapshot for our review.

Can you provide an index of the artifacts you can share, any redaction constraints, and an estimated timeline? Ideally we need materials by COB Monday so our information security team can start triage.

Appreciate it —
Elena

Elena Ruiz
Senior InfoSec Analyst, HarborBank
elena.ruiz@harborbank.com

[Attachment: harborbank_rfp_vm_questions.pdf]

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@harborbank.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 17:12:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Vendor evidence for vulnerability management questionnaire

Elena —

Thanks for the clear list. We can provide the following within the timeframe you requested: an evidence index (what we can share vs. redacted), our SAST/DAST tooling list and coverage notes, patch SLA matrix by CVE severity, a redacted pen-test executive summary, and an SBOM export (CSV).

Quick notes up front:
- SAST: internal pipeline using two engines (open-source + commercial) for PR gates and pre-prod scans; we run scheduled full scans weekly for service code and on every merge to main.
- DAST: auth-scoped DAST in staging for public endpoints with authenticated runs nightly against canary stacks; we also run targeted regression scans for releases impacting customer-facing routes.
- Patch SLA: our operational target is 48 hours for critical (CVSS >=9.0) fixes once exploitability is confirmed, 7 days for high, 30 days for medium, and quarterly for low/informational items unless otherwise escalated. We capture exceptions in change control.

I'll attach the evidence index and an initial SBOM CSV. Neha and Marcus are looped in to provide the pen-test summary and the formal SAST/DAST configuration notes.

Next steps: we will upload the redacted pen-test summary to a secure share and provide a short readout (30 min) if HarborBank wants a walkthrough.

Best,
Mina
Mina Haddad
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: vm_evidence_index.md] [Attachment: redwood_sbom_v2.csv]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@harborbank.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:45:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Vendor evidence for vulnerability management questionnaire

Elena / team —

Attaching a short pen-test executive summary (PDF, redacted) and a patch SLA matrix (XLSX). A few clarifications to the SAST/DAST section in the questionnaire:

SAST specifics:
- Engines: CodeGuard OSS (open-source) + GuardProbe Enterprise for taint analysis and custom rules.
- Coverage: ~92% branch coverage on service codebase; ruleset includes CWE mapping and tailored rules for Redwood runtime.
- False-positive handling: triage within 24 hours of triage queue entry; developers have SLA to respond/comment within 5 business days.

DAST specifics:
- Scanning cadence: nightly authenticated scans in staging for canonical customer routes; on-demand for release windows.
- Authenticated scanning uses a dedicated scan account with limited privileges.
- Findings triaged into JIRA; remediation SLAs align with patch SLA matrix.

Pen test summary highlights:
- Last full pen test: July 2026 by third-party firm BlueCrest Security.
- No critical issues found; two high-severity findings (one JSON injection pattern, one misconfigured CORS policy) were patched within 36 and 22 hours respectively.
- Remaining medium findings are tracked with remediation plans and ETA in JIRA.

Im attaching the redacted PDF and the SLA matrix. We can provide full technical details under NDA if needed.

Marcus
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: pen_test_summary_aug2026_redacted.pdf] [Attachment: patch_sla_matrix_v1.xlsx]

From: Tom Mitchell <tom.mitchell@harborbank.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@harborbank.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 10:20:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Vendor evidence for vulnerability management questionnaire

Thanks Mina / Marcus — quick follow-ups from InfoSec:

1) On the pen test summary: can you confirm whether BlueCrest executed authenticated tests that exercised internal APIs behind the gateway, or were tests limited to the public surface? We need a short note on test scope.
2) For SBOM: is the CSV a component-level SBOM with version pins, or a service-level inventory? We want component-level listings for supply-chain review.
3) Patch SLA: can you provide a concrete example of the ticket lifecycle for a critical CVE (from detection to verification)? They want to see timestamps in a sample ticket.

If you can supply answers and the additional sample ticket by end of day, we can proceed to our risk committee review.

—Tom
Director, Third-Party Risk, HarborBank

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Mitchell <tom.mitchell@harborbank.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@harborbank.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 16:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Vendor evidence for vulnerability management questionnaire

Tom / Elena —

Answers below and attached sample ticket (redacted):

1) Pen test scope: BlueCrest performed both unauthenticated external surface testing and authenticated API testing that exercised internal API endpoints routed via our gateway. Authenticated tests used scoped service accounts and included tests of microservice-to-microservice calls where applicable. Statement of scope is in the attached pen-test executive summary.

2) SBOM: the attached CSV is a component-level SBOM exported from our build system with package names, versions, license, and source repo references. We also produce a higher-level service inventory mapping which we can provide separately.

3) Sample critical ticket lifecycle (redacted):
- 2026-07-15 09:12: detection (internal SCA alert + ingestion of public CVE feed)
- 2026-07-15 11:05: triage (confirmed exploitability, severity = critical)
- 2026-07-15 13:40: patch deployed to canary clusters
- 2026-07-15 18:20: patch promoted to prod and verification completed
- 2026-07-15 20:05: ticket closed after QA verification and post-deploy scan

We attach the redacted ticket PDF and the SBOM CSV. If HarborBank wants, we can schedule a 30-min walkthrough of the pen-test findings and our ticketing workflow this week.

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
